headline: Siakam and Nesmith power the Pacers to a 106-104 win over the Knicks
text: INDIANAPOLIS -- — Pascal Siakam scored 19 points and Aaron Nesmith added 18 to lead the Indiana Pacers to a 106-104 win over the New York Knicks in an NBA Cup game on Friday night. Siakam's 15-foot jumper with 1:49 remaining gave Indiana a 106-98 lead before the Knicks stormed back. Jalen Brunson’s driving layup cut the lead to 106-102 with 26 seconds left. Siakam was fouled, but missed both free throws with 23 seconds left. Mikal Bridges scored to slice the lead to two points with 10 seconds to go before the Pacers turned the ball over with 2.8 seconds to go. But, Karl-Anthony Towns missed a potential game-tying 15-foot jumper at the buzzer. Nesmith, who was limited to 21 minutes because of right knee soreness in Wednesday’s victory over Washington, was declared available earlier Friday. Kelly Oubre Jr . scored 16 points and Ivica Zubac had 12 points and 13 rebounds for Indiana. Brunson led he Knicks with 33 points. Towns finished with 23 points and 15 rebounds and Bridges added 18 for the Knicks. Both teams shot 43%. Indiana held a 50-43 edge in rebounds. With the Pacers leading 85-74, the Knicks went on a 10-0 run to narrow the deficit to 85-84 after three quarters. For the game, the Pacers shot 18 of 25 from the line. New York made 10 of 13. Up next Knicks: At Toronto on Sunday. Pacers: At Philadelphia on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Wagner falls a rebound shy of a triple-double in the Magic's 107-99 win over the Bucks
text: ORLANDO, Fla. -- — Franz Wagner fell a rebound shy of his first career triple-double, scoring 35 points and adding 12 assists to lead the Orlando Magic to their first home victory, 107-99 over the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday night in NBA Cup play. Desmond Bane added 21 points to help Orlando improve to 2-0 in NBA Cup group play. Milwaukee fell to 0-2 in the group that also includes Brooklyn, Detroit and Toronto. Tyler Herro had 18 points for Milwaukee, which lost a ninth straight game to equal its longest streak since a nine-game slide Jan. 2-19, 2014. Per Sportradar, the Bucks (1-12) are off to their worst start in 52 years, when they lost 13 of their first 14 in 1974-75 without an injured Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Wagner made a turnaround hook with six minutes left to reach 30 points in a fourth consecutive game. And when the Bucks were within eight in the final minute, Wagner stole the ball and used a Euro-step layup to give Orlando a 104-94 advantage. He finished with nine rebounds. The Magic also got a season-high 12 points from Goga Bitadze , half on alley-oop dunks off Wagner's passes. Tristan da Silva , who missed two games with a calf injury, returned to the lineup and also had 12 points. Up next Bucks: Hosts Atlanta on Sunday night. Magic: At Boston on Monday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Adebayo, Antetokounmpo make Heat history, Miami tops Cleveland 133-121 in NBA Cup game
text: MIAMI -- — Bam Adebayo finished with 37 points and 14 rebounds, Giannis Antetokiunmpo also scored 37 and the Miami Heat took control of East Group B by beating the Cleveland Cavaliers 133-121 in an NBA Cup game Friday night. It was the second time the Heat had two players score 37 in the same game: LeBron James and Dwyane Wade did it in 2013. Davion Mitchell had 22 points and a career-high-tying 17 assists for Miami, which won its third straight. Ryan Conwell added 20 off the bench for the Heat. Donovan Mitchell scored 25 points to lead Cleveland, which got 22 from Tyrese Proctor , 20 from James Harden , 16 from Jaylon Tyson and 12 from Meleek Thomas . Miami was without Klay Thompson (sprained ankle) and Pelle Larsson (illness). Cleveland played without forward Evan Mobley , who sat out for the first time this season with a sprained left great toe. "The MRI came back clean. Sprained, definitely sore, but we don't expect it to be a long-term thing at all,” Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson said. With the win, the Heat move to 2-0 and are now alone atop East Group B in the NBA Cup standings. They control their destiny now when it comes to making the knockout stage; a sweep of remaining group-stage games against Philadelphia and New York — both on the road — would get Miami into the quarterfinals. Even going 1-1 in those matchups would give the Heat a solid shot at a wild-card berth. Cleveland falls to 1-1 in group play and will almost certainly need to win both of its remaining games — home against Indiana, then at New York — to have a shot at advancing. No team in NBA Cup history has made the knockout stage with less than a 3-1 record in group play. Up next Cavaliers: Host Dallas on Saturday. Heat: Host Detroit on Saturday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Powell scores 33 as the Bulls snap 8-game skid, beating the Hawks 125-117 in OT
text: CHICAGO -- — Norman Powell scored nine of his 33 points in overtime and the Chicago Bulls snapped an eight-game skid with a 125-117 victory over the Atlanta Hawks in an NBA Cup game Friday night. Josh Giddey had 14 assists and 10 rebounds, and joined Jalen Smith (12 rebounds) and Isaac Okoro with 15 points apiece for Chicago, which entered having lost nine of its 10 games this season. The Bulls' only other win came at Milwaukee on Oct. 23. Patrick Williams scored 13 points, Buddy Hield added 12 and Matas Buzelis 11 as Chicago snapped a four-game home losing streak. Jalen Johnson had 16 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists for the Hawks, who trailed by seven points at halftime. CJ McCollum scored 20 points, Onyeka Okongwu chipped in 17 and Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 16 for Atlanta. Jock Landale (12 points) and Luguentz Dort (10) also scored in double figures. Atlanta, which entered having won four of its last five games, dropped its second straight after a 124-114 decision to the Los Angeles Lakers on Monday. Up next Hawks: At the Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday night. Bulls: At the Minnesota Timberwolves on Saturday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Grizzlies have record-tying 10 double-figure scorers in 142-111 romp over Pelicans in NBA Cup play
text: NEW ORLEANS -- — Jerami Grant scored 22 points, including seven points on an extended possession in the first half, and the Memphis Grizzlies routed the New Orleans Pelicans 142-111 in NBA Cup group play Friday night. The Grizzlies matched an NBA record with 10 players in double figures in scoring. Ty Jerome had 17, Cedric Coward , GG Jackson and Cam Spencer added 14 each, Isaiah Stewart and Cam Boozer each had 12, Jaylen Wells scored 11, and Taylor Hendricks and Javon Small had 10 each. In winning their sixth consecutive road game — the best road record in the NBA and the best road start in franchise history — the Grizzlies overwhelmed the Pelicans with their perimeter shooting, finishing 18 of 45 from 3-point range while holding New Orleans to 7 of 31. The Grizzlies improved their NBA Cup record to 1-1 in the West’s Group B, and the Pelicans dropped to 0-2. The Grizzlies scored 13 consecutive points in a 1:07 span of the second quarter to build a 62-46 lead. Grant had seven points in seven seconds, nailing a pair of 3s and adding a foul shot after Zion Williamson was called for an illegal closeout.. Grant left with 7:36 left after colliding with Herb Jones on a head-first drive to the basket. Saddiq Bey led New Orleans with 30 points, the first Pelican to score more than 30 points this season. Williamson had 22 points, five rebounds and three steals. Memphis led 70-58 at the half and then 105-86 after three, stringing together three consecutive 35-point quarters. They added a 37-point fourth quarter to complete the rout. Up next Grizzlies: Host Brooklyn on Saturday night. Pelicans: Host Denver on Saturday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Alperin Sengun scores 43 points to power Rockets past skidding Jazz 125-118
text: HOUSTON -- — Alperin Sengun scored 43 points and pulled down 12 rebounds as the Houston Rockets held off Utah 125-118 in NBA Cup play Friday night, handing the Jazz their 11th consecutive loss. It was Sengun's second career 40-point game, and he did it on an efficient 17 of 24 from the floor. The Rockets (10-3) needed the boost with Kevin Durant — 22 points on 5 of 14 from the field — having a tough shooting night. Sengun's other 40-point game came in 2024 when he posted a career-high 45 against the San Antonio Spurs . The teams were tied at 27 after the first quarter, but Sengun's nine points in the second helped the Rockets take a 63-53 lead into halftime. The Jazz (1-12) made a dent in the deficit, with Keyonte George scoring 10 of his 27 points in the third quarter to cut Houston's advantage to 92-89 after three. Utah was able to keep it close the rest of the way, getting within two possessions in the final minute, but Durant iced the game with a pair of free throws in the closing seconds. Darryn Peterson led the Jazz with 28 points and Ace Bailey added 21. Utah's only win came in its second game of the season, against New Orleans. Houston has won its last three and is 1-1 in NBA Cup play, with two group-stage games remaining. Up next Jazz: Host the Spurs on Sunday. Rockets: Play at Washington on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Castle scores season-high 32 points as Spurs stop the Warriors 123-85 for 11th straight win
text: SAN ANTONIO -- — Stephon Castle scored a season-high 32 points, Victor Wembanyama had 12 points and 12 rebounds and the San Antonio Spurs won their 11th straight game, rolling past the Golden State Warriors 123-85 Friday night to remain unbeaten in NBA Cup play. Golden State's only double-figure scorers were L.J. Cryer with 20 points and Charles Bassey with 11. The Warriors are without Stephen Curry , who is sidelined at least two weeks with a right oblique tear suffered in a 115-108 loss in Houston on Wednesday. Golden State could have used a banner scoring night from the two-time MVP to overcome this lopsided loss. The Spurs led by 43 points in the third quarter, allowing the defending Western Conference champions to sit their starters and most of their key reserves for the entire fourth. Wembanyama was 5 for 11 from the field and 0 for 2 on 3-pointers while playing only 21 minutes and collecting his 121st career double-double. Warriors forward Draymond Green was issued a Flagrant Foul 1 for a forearm shove from behind off a running start that sent Wembanyama tumbling out of bounds with 6:47 remaining in the first half. Green, who exited and did not return in the first half after the Flagrant 1, finished with four points, three rebounds and three assists in 16 minutes. Golden State was 5 for 25 from the field in the opening quarter as San Antonio raced to a 38-14 lead. It was the fewest points scored in any quarter by a Spurs opponent this season, as well as a season low for the Warriors. Golden State trailed 63-33 at the half, the fewest points by a San Antonio opponent in the first half since Phoenix had 31 on Feb. 7, 2018. Castle shot 12 for 18 and was 5 for 8 on 3-pointers. He surpassed his previous high of 24 points against Oklahoma City on opening night on a slam dunk off an alley-oop pass on a finger roll from Wembanyama. Up next Warriors: At New Orleans on Monday. Spurs: At Utah on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Trail Blazers beat Kings 120-107 in NBA Cup play for third straight win
text: SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Deni Avdija scored 34 points and the Portland Trail Blazers beat the Sacramento Kings 120-107 on Friday night in NBA Cup play to open a six-game trip with their third straight victory. Damian Lillard added 29 points to help Portland improve to 9-3. The Trail Blazers are 6-1 on the road, with the lone loss to the Los Angeles Lakers in their NBA Cup opener. Avdija was 11 of 13 from the field, hitting 3 of 5 3-pointers, and nine free throws without a miss. Toumani Camara added 14 points for Portland, and Donovan Clingan had 13 points and 11 rebounds. De’Andre Hunter led Sacramento with 24 points. The Kings have lost five in a row to fall to 1-11 overall and 0-7 at home. Domantas Sabonis had 21 points and 12 rebounds. Up next Trail Blazers: At Minnesota on Monday and Tuesday nights. Kings: Host Oklahoma City of Sunday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Clippers overcome 40 points from SGA and use late run to slip past Thunder 113-112
text: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Brook Lopez scored 26 points and Darius Garland added 24 as the Los Angeles Clippers finished off a 113-112 victory Friday night in an NBA Cup game, sending the short-handed Oklahoma City Thunder to a season-high third straight loss. Derrick Jones Jr . and rookie Keaton Wagler had 14 points apiece, and Gradey Dick added 13 as the Clippers scored the final seven points to win for the second time in three games after opening the season with a 1-7 record. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 40 for the Thunder but missed a 21-foot jumper at the buzzer that would have won it. Jared McCain had 23 points and Isaiah Hartenstein added 21 points with 16 rebounds as Oklahoma City fell to 0-3 on a four-game West Coast trip. McCain finished 7 of 11 from 3-point range. The Clippers led 57-44 at halftime behind 12 points from Lopez, while the Thunder were just 2 of 17 on 3s over the first two quarters. Oklahoma City recovered to outscore Los Angeles 40-25 in the third by going 5 of 11 from long distance. Gilgeous-Alexander hit a leaning 3-pointer with 3:01 remaining for a 110-106 lead. The Clippers trailed 112-106 with 2:43 remaining before closing the game on a 7-0 run. Lopez scored a pair of baskets down the stretch before Garland put the Clippers ahead for good on a three-point play with 50.4 seconds left. Without starters Chet Holmgren (knee), Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) since Oct. 26, the Thunder started a pair of 7-footers in Hartenstein and rookie Aday Mara for the second consecutive game and fourth time this season. Mara finished with 10 points and three blocks. Up next Thunder: At Sacramento on Sunday. Clippers: Home vs. Charlotte on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
